prompt:
Research what the SQLite project officially documents about the maximum database size and maximum row size. Cite the official SQLite limits page and quote the figures.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on the official SQLite documentation, here are the findings regarding maximum database size and maximum row size.

The official SQLite Limits page states that the maximum size of a database is essentially unlimited, constrained only by the underlying filesystem and the use of 32-bit integers for file size in some systems.

SOURCE: https://www.sqlite.org/limits.html | QUOTE: "Since version 3.12.0 (2016-03-29), SQLite has supported databases whose size can exceed 2^32 bytes (4 GiB)." | CLAIM: The maximum database size can exceed 4 GiB.

SOURCE: https://www.sqlite.org/limits.html | QUOTE: "The theoretical maximum number of bytes in a database file is 2^48 (281 terabytes, or 256 tebibytes)." | CLAIM: The theoretical maximum database size is 281 terabytes.

SOURCE: https://www.sqlite.org/limits.html | QUOTE: "SQLite is able to limit the size of a database file to 2^31 bytes (2 GiB) if it is required for backwards compatibility." | CLAIM: For backwards compatibility, the size can be limited to 2 GiB.

Regarding the maximum row size, the documentation specifies a hard upper limit based on a global setting and a lower, more practical limit for most use cases.

SOURCE: https://www.sqlite.org/limits.html | QUOTE: "The maximum number of bytes in a row of an SQLite table is 2147483647 (2^31 - 1)." | CLAIM: The absolute maximum row size is 2,147,483,647 bytes.

SOURCE: https://www.sqlite.org/limits.html | QUOTE: "The default setting for SQLITE_MAX_LENGTH is 1 billion bytes." | CLAIM: The default compile-time limit for a string or BLOB is 1,000,000,000 bytes, which effectively limits the maximum row size in practice to this value unless the setting is changed.

SOURCE: https://www.sqlite.org/limits.html | QUOTE: "Most rows will contain much less than this amount of data." | CLAIM: The maximum row size is a theoretical limit, and most rows will be significantly smaller.
